newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand set to scrap Hopewell project.
newsitem.headline: Thailand set to scrap Hopewell project.

text.p: Thailand is moving to scrap a 30-year concession for Hopewell Holdings Ltd to build and operate a Bangkok multi-level rail and highway network at the end of July because the company has indicated it could not arrange financing for the project, a government official said on Thursday.

Sathien Wongvichien, deputy permanent secretary for transport and communications, said the Thai government could exercise its contractual right to scrap the concession awarded to Hopewell in 1990 as the firm has failed to meet its obligations.

"If (Hopewell) cannot come up with a firm financing package by the end of July, the communications ministry can scrap the contract...up until now, it has failed to meet construction schedules in completing Phase One in time for the Bangkok Asian Games in late 1998," Sathien said.
Hopewell chairman Gordon Wu said early this week the de facto devaluation of the Thai baht had raised the project cost by 15 percent.
Before the baht depreciated by 20 percent since early this month, Hopewell's 60-km (37.5-mile) project was estimated to cost US$3.2 billion.
Sathien said the government would probably find new investors to carry on the long-delayed project, with Hopewell scaling down its role from project operator to its future shareholder.
Thai officials said less than 20 percent of the project's 40-km (25-mile) first phase had been completed more than seven years after the government and Hopewell signed the project contract.
